BiblicalUsage: ʻeseb means grass. It turns up in Exodus, Deuteronomy, and Psalms, and the sense holds steady from place to place. It is a plain word, and that plainness is the point: Scripture does not dress it up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʻeseb matters because it names something Scripture keeps returning to. So I hold the meaning steady and let the context do the rest.
RelatedEvents: The Ten Plagues; The Plague of Hail
